newsitem.title: UK: De Silguy won't rule out softer EMU rules, British paper says.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy won't rule out softer EMU rules, British paper says.

text.p: European Economics Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy declined to rule out the possibility that countries with deficits above three percent of their gross domestic product would launch the single European currency, the Daily Telegraph reported.

"I can't answer for one criteria without all the elements - to be able to appreciate if we have a high degree of sustainable convergence," he said in an interview published in Friday's Daily Telegraph when asked if a country with a deficit of 3.5 percent of its GDP could join economic and monetary union.

He said countries wishing to join EMU would have to be close to the reference values set out in the Maastricht treaty but added that he wanted a "strict but not stupid" application of the entry criteria, the UK newspaper reported.
The treaty specifies a deficit to GDP ratio of three percent for EMU entrants.
De Silguy warned that a delay to the project would be "a catastrophe" and said the single currency would benefit Europe.
